Two papers in the library propose a preference-optimisation method built to work without a reference model. A third tests a no-reference variant as a side experiment.

**1. ORPO: Monolithic Preference Optimization without Reference Model**
(`llm/post-training/preference-learning/`)
- The abstract presents ORPO as a "reference model-free monolithic odds ratio preference optimization algorithm" that removes the need for a separate preference-alignment phase (p. 1).
- Figure 2 shows ORPO aligning the model without a reference model, unlike RLHF and DPO (p. 2).
- It contrasts favoured and disfavoured responses using the odds ratio, added to the usual fine-tuning loss (p. 1).
- The conclusion calls it "a reference-free monolithic preference alignment method" (p. 9).

**2. SimPO: Simple Preference Optimization with a Reference-Free Reward**
(`llm/post-training/preference-learning/`)
- The abstract says SimPO's reward is aligned with generation and "eliminates the need for a reference model, making it more compute and memory efficient" (p. 1). Listing "Simplicity" as a contribution, the paper repeats that it needs no reference model (p. 2).
- It argues that DPO needs a reference model during training, which adds memory and compute cost (p. 3). SimPO instead uses the average log-likelihood of a response as its reward, so no reference model is needed (pp. 3–4). It also adds a target reward margin (p. 4).
- Dropping the reference model's forward passes cuts run time and per-GPU memory use by about 10% (p. 10).
- SimPO itself names ORPO as another recent reference-free objective (p. 2).

**Partial case: KTO: Model Alignment as Prospect Theoretic Optimization**
- KTO's main method uses a reference model (p. 3), so it is not a reference-free proposal.
- The paper does test a reference-free variant. It assumes the reference model gives a uniform distribution, which saves memory. This variant "works without a reference model or SFT, but not as well as standard KTO" (p. 8). Results for this "no πref" variant appear in Table 2 (p. 8) and are defined on p. 18.

Several surveys and other papers in the library also mention reference-free methods, such as the DPO survey and Tulu 3. However, they only discuss or cite such methods rather than propose one, so I left them out.
